title: Classify PR commits by content in pr_commits, not Athena-Job trailers
summary: Rewrite `pr_commits` in athena-core land.rs to classify each commit in `remote_base..head` by what it changes (records_only, declared_intervention, job_landing), so `athena land --pr` stops refusing real PRs. The job_landing rule follows the gate's closing_jobs, which includes a blocked job that is later landed by a commit adding only outcome-landed.json. The audience is Sri and the verifier.

defaults_applied.how: New land tests plus clippy and fmt criteria.
The criteria run the realistic, blocked-then-landed and refusal ranges.
The trailer dependence is removed, not given exceptions.
One focused change in pr_commits and its caller.
Doc comments and the design doc state the rules.
An empty range is still an error.
BRIEF.md asks for tagged releases and a changelog, so the change records itself in CHANGELOG.md.

assumptions: Goal: real PRs that Athena lands stop being refused for missing Athena-Job trailers. Audience: Sri and the verifier running the athena-core land and gh tests.
LandingCommit's kind field, added in b6f22c2, already exists. gh.rs currently hard-codes JobLanding.
invariant.rs may need small visibility changes (pub(crate)/pub) to share closing_jobs, not_landed and the CLOSING list with athena-core.
The previous attempt failed on requiring all three closing files in one commit. This reading relaxes that, per the critic and the introspection.

operator/ is Governed in this repo, since .gitattributes excludes only /CLAUDE.md, /BRIEF.md and /LICENSE. The fixture mirrors the real attributes. A lease commit that changes the fingerprint is refused unless it is an owner path. The tests state which case they show.
Test runs are limited to athena-core land and gh, plus a narrow gate invariant run only if invariant.rs changes.

acceptance_criteria.text: Run `cargo test -p athena-core land::`. A realistic-range test uses a fixture with this repo's real .gitattributes (no extra operator/ exclusion) and builds: reading, dispatch and introspection commits, a lease commit under operator/, an intervention commit adding records/interventions/<month>/<id>.json, then the job's landing adding candidate, verification and outcome. No commit has an Athena-Job trailer. It asserts kinds in order: records_only for the first four, declared_intervention, then job_landing with that job and verification id. If operator/ is governed in this repo, the fixture marks it as an owner path the way the real repo does. The test's doc comment names the fixture's .gitattributes lines.

Run `cargo test -p athena-core land::`. A blocked-then-landed test has a commit adding candidate, verification and a blocked outcome (records_only), then a commit adding only outcome-landed.json plus governed work. It yields RecordsOnly then JobLanding for that job with its verification id.

Run `cargo test -p athena-core land::`. Refusal tests: (a) a commit that changes governed content without being an intervention or a job's closing records, (b) a landing with a missing verification, and (c) a landing whose outcome is not landed each make `pr_commits` return an error containing that commit's sha. A companion assertion shows that an operator/ lease commit is refused with its sha when operator/ is governed, so the real-repo behavior is shown.
Run `cargo test -p athena-core gh::`. The gh tests pass. The commits built for a Landing record carry the kind from `pr_commits` instead of a hard-coded JobLanding and pass `LandingCommit::validate`.

`pr_commits` and `PrCommit` no longer read trailers or mention Athena-Job. `PrCommit` carries kind, optional job and optional verification. Doc comments state the content rules: records_only when the fingerprint equals the parent's, using the gate's `fingerprint(git, commit, base)`; job_landing when the commit adds a landed outcome for exactly one request job and that job's candidate and verification exist in the commit's tree. The rule reuses the gate's closing_jobs/not_landed logic, so there is a single source of truth.

An empty range is still an error. The old trailer-count tests are removed, not left alongside the new ones. The change description lists every writer of landing records (including run.rs retry_landing) and the test that covers each. It also says why a narrow `cargo test -p athena-gate invariant` was run, if one was.
Run `cargo clippy -p athena-core --all-targets` and `cargo fmt --check`. Both are clean.
docs/design/records-history.md §5.3 and CHANGELOG.md describe the content-based classification and no longer describe the trailer rule.

out_of_scope: Changing the gate's own landing invariant semantics
Running tests beyond athena-core land and gh (apart from a narrow gate invariant run if needed)
departures: Higher than the reference. The earlier attempts timed out or failed in planning, the change touches several crates, and the commit-shape fixtures are intricate.
